Clinical outcome: Confirmed responses in 11/38 evaluable patients; 40 received IMA203.
Adverse events: CRS, cytopenias and mild/moderate ICANS occurred; one reported DLT. No specific renal toxicity reported despite weak in-vitro reactivity in one renal donor.
Review depth: Primary full-text clinical results and specificity sections; primary adrenal-IHC abstract.
Limitations: Accepted low adrenal-cortical protein remains true. The selected peptide was not quantifiable in 41 tested normal tissue types; non-detection is assay-limited. No clearance of other PRAME peptides or receptors.
Rationale: Low-level normal protein does not automatically prohibit research selection when the measured RNA gates pass and a directly tested selective product has repeated prospective tumor responses. Retain the adrenal finding and product scope.

Product: Afamitresgene autoleucel / TECELRA; indication- and HLA-restricted
Clinical outcome: SPEARHEAD-1 cohort 1: 19/52 objective responses; approved product in defined synovial-sarcoma population.
Adverse events: CRS and severe cytopenias are documented; product labelling includes serious risks. Trial abstract reports no treatment-related deaths in cohort 1.
Review depth: Primary assay-validation full text; primary phase-2 abstract; FDA product indication and label warning review.
Limitations: OTI1F9 normal panel negative outside testis/placenta; minor experimental cross-reactivity is reported. It does not prove HPA021942/CAB040535 stains false. Raw staining remains unresolved; approval does not validate every MAGE-A4 receptor.
Rationale: Prospective repeated responses plus a separately validated normal-tissue assay support research selection despite unconfirmed raw-antibody conflicts; retain every conflict as a qualification.

Product: NY-ESO-1-reactive TCR; shared antigen encoded by CTAG1A/B
Clinical outcome: Responses in 11/18 synovial-sarcoma and 11/20 melanoma patients in the reported follow-up.
Adverse events: Clinical regimen toxicity requires product-level assessment; no inference of universal tolerability.
Review depth: Primary abstract; carried-forward reference-bound expression review.
Limitations: Clinical NY-ESO-1 antigen evidence is shared between the two loci and is not independent replication. No new whole-proteome specificity review claimed.
Rationale: Retained by measured expression evidence; clinical antigen evidence is supportive and does not distinguish the two encoding loci.

Clinical outcome: 16 treated; no RECIST objective response. Stable disease and individual lesion shrinkage are not objective responses.
Adverse events: Cytopenias, CRS including one grade-3 event, and grade-1 ICANS reported.
Review depth: Primary full-text abstract, safety and clinical-response results; carried-forward antibody review.
Limitations: Biological activity and manageable product safety do not establish repeated clinical responses; raw normal staining remains unresolved.
Rationale: This comparator does not meet the repeated-objective-response evidence criterion; do not promote on trial registration or stable disease.

Clinical outcome: NSCLC cohort: one partial response after repeat infusion among 11 treated; other phase-1 tumor cohort did not establish repeated responses.
Adverse events: CRS, cytopenias and a death after repeat infusion/intensified lymphodepletion are documented. Do not attribute death uniquely to antigen targeting.
Review depth: Primary NSCLC full-text results and discussion; second-cohort abstract; carried-forward antibody review.
Limitations: A single response with a complicated regimen is not comparable evidence to repeated responses; normal-antibody conflicts remain unresolved.
Rationale: This comparator fails repeated-response qualification; preserve its clinical experience without upgrading eligibility.
